## Teaching points

1. Compare sodium with its baseline and reconcile recent prescriptions. Withhold the suspected drug and observe symptoms, urine output and serial electrolytes; correction can accelerate after stopping a thiazide.
2. A recent normal sodium and new thiazide exposure are useful clues, but evaluate other contributors and the severity of symptoms.
3. Sodium is not a treatment-responsive variable in this engine. No automatic correction is scripted; the clinical plan must include serial monitoring and avoidance of overcorrection.
